chapters.title: Ch1 Real Numbers

concept.anchor: Sharing laddoos equally — Euclid's division is dividing a big box of laddoos into equal packets without breaking any.
concept.ncert: Euclid's Division Lemma: a = bq + r, 0 ≤ r < b. Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic: every composite n >1 is unique product of primes. HCF via prime factorization, LCM relation.
concept.bridge: RD: Prove √2, √3 irrational by contradiction; decimal expansions — terminating iff denominator = 2^m·5^n.

formulae: If p|a² then p|a (for prime p)
dailyLife: Dividing 2 chocolate bars among 3 friends fairly
Finding when 2 buses (every 15/20 min) meet again — LCM
frontier: Cryptography: prime factorization secures UPI/ISRO links
GPS signal cycles use Euclid-like remainders
Rocket staging: LCM of orbits for launch windows

theoremsDetailed.name: Euclid's Division Lemma

theoremsDetailed.name: Euclid's Algorithm
theoremsDetailed.statement: Repeated lemma until r=0, last divisor is HCF
theoremsDetailed.derivation: Algorithm steps: a=bq+r → b=rq1+r1 → ... → r_n=0, HCF=r_{n-1}. Example 18 & 30 → 6.

theoremsDetailed.name: Fundamental Theorem
theoremsDetailed.derivation: Existence via induction, uniqueness via Euclid's lemma (if p|ab then p|a or p|b). Visual: factor tree for 36 and 3825.

theoremsDetailed.name: Product Relation
theoremsDetailed.derivation: Via prime factors: HCF = common, LCM = common·uncommon, product = common²·uncommon = HCF·LCM.

theoremsDetailed.name: Irrational √p
theoremsDetailed.derivation: Contradiction: assume √p=a/b coprime → a²=pb² → p|a → a=pc → p|b contradiction.
theoremsDetailed.visualization: Detective board

theoremsDetailed.name: Terminating Test
theoremsDetailed.statement: a/b terminates iff b=2^m·5^n after reducing

sections.title: Real Numbers — The Complete Picture
sections.content: Any number except complex is real: -1, 1/2, 1.75, √2. Real = Rational ∪ Irrational. Every real lives on the number line. Visual: Real Numbers Chart (Natural ⊂ Whole ⊂ Integers ⊂ Rational ⊂ Real, with Irrational separate) — garden diagram, soft shadows, Tiranga accent, not clip art.
sections.visual: Real Numbers Chart — interactive, hover to highlight subsets

sections.title: Euclid's Division Lemma
sections.content: Given a,b integers, exists unique q,r with a = b·q + r, 0 ≤ r < b. Essentially dividend = divisor·quotient + remainder. Unique q,r — the engine behind HCF.
sections.visual: Garden division: 65 laddoos ÷ 13 packets — Euclid's lemma as sharing, 20s animation building q,r

sections.title: Euclid's Division Algorithm
sections.content: Repeated lemma: a = b·q + r → if r=0, HCF=b else replace (b,r) and repeat until r=0. Divisor at last step is HCF. Example: HCF(18,30) → 30=18·1+12, 18=12·1+6, 12=6·2+0 → HCF 6.
sections.visual: Step ladder: 30→18→12→6, each step highlights divisor/remainder, 3-min movie-like

sections.title: Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic
sections.content: Every composite n>1 is product of primes, unique up to order. 36=2·2·3·3 =2·3·2·3 — same primes, different order, unique set. Prime factorisation is the prime bricks.
sections.visual: Factor tree for 36 and 3825=3²·5²·17, bricks stacking, 20s morph

sections.title: LCM & HCF — Two Methods, One Relation
sections.content: LCM: smallest common multiple via prime factors (common × uncommon). HCF: greatest common divisor via prime factors (common) or Euclid's algorithm. Relation: For two numbers a·b = HCF·LCM (not for 3+). Example: 36 & 56 → HCF 4, LCM 504, 36·56=2016=4·504. Applications: bells ringing together, persons meeting — LCM finds common occurrence.
sections.visual: Side-by-side: prime factor cards for 36 (2·2·3·3) and 56 (2·2·2·7) → common 2·2 highlighted, LCM built as 2·2·3·3·2·7

sections.title: Irrational Numbers & Proof by Contradiction
sections.content: Irrational = not p/q (q≠0): √2, π, e. Key results: if prime p|a² then p|a; sum/difference of rational+irrational is irrational; √p is irrational for prime p. Proof: Assume √7 = a/b coprime → a²=7b² → 7|a → a=7c → 7b²=49c² → 7|b contradiction → √7 irrational. Same for 1/√2.
sections.visual: Proof by contradiction as detective story: assume → deduce → contradiction → boxed, with garden detective board

sections.title: Rational Numbers & Decimal Expansions
sections.content: Rational = p/q, q≠0. Decimal: terminating (ends, e.g., 0.025) vs non-terminating (0.333…, 0.142857… recurring vs π non-recurring). Test: a/b terminates iff after reducing (HCF=1), b=2^m·5^n (only 2s and 5s). Example: 1/40=0.025 (40=2³·5) terminates, 3/7=0.428571… (7=7¹) recurs.
sections.visual: Denominator prime factor filter: 2s & 5s pass (green), other prime (red) → recurring, 20s animation

solvedExamples.q: Find largest number dividing 70 and 125 leaving remainders 5 and 8
solvedExamples.solution: Subtract remainders: 65 & 117 → HCF(65,117). 65=5·13, 117=3·3·13 → HCF 13 → Answer 13. Multiple: Euclid's algorithm also gives 13 in 3 steps. Shortcut: remainders first, then prime factors in 30s.
solvedExamples.visual: Garden sharing: 70-5, 125-8 → common divisor as largest packet

solvedExamples.q: Find LCM of 306 and 657 given HCF=9
solvedExamples.solution: Use a·b=HCF·LCM → 306·657=9·LCM → LCM=201042/9=22338. Visual: product relation as balance scale.
Assume 1/√2=p/q coprime → q/p=√2 rational → √2 rational contradiction (since √2 irrational) → 1/√2 irrational. Alternative: direct √2 proof then reciprocal.
solvedExamples.visual: Contradiction board: assume → q/p=√2 → √2 rational → clash

sections.title: Algebraic Expressions — Building Blocks
sections.content: Expression = sum of terms; term = constant·variables. Example: 3x²y+4xy+5x+6 has four terms: 3x²y, 4xy, 5x, 6. Coefficient is constant in term. Exponent on variable must be rational for algebraic, but for polynomial it must be whole number (0,1,2...). 5x³+3x+1 is polynomial; 2x+3√x is algebraic but NOT polynomial (exponent 1/2).
sections.visual: Blocks: 3x²y as 3·x·x·y, 4xy, 5x, 6 — garden bricks stacking, 20s build

sections.title: Polynomial — Whole-Number Exponents Only
sections.content: Polynomial requires whole-number exponents. 5x³+3x+1 ✅, 2x+3√x ❌ (1/2). Degree = highest exponent on variable. x²+2x+3 degree 2, x⁸+2x⁶-3x+9 degree 8.
sections.visual: Filter: rational vs whole-number exponents — whole pass (green), rational fail (amber), 20s

sections.title: Types — By Terms & Degree
sections.content: By terms: monomial (1 term: 2x), binomial (2: 4x²+x), trinomial (3: x²+3x+4). By degree: linear (1: 2x+1), quadratic (2: 3x²+8x+5), cubic (3: 2x³+5x²+9x+15).
sections.visual: Cards: monomial/binomial/trinomial + linear/quadratic/cubic with degree badge

sections.title: Graphical Representation — Where Zeroes Live
sections.content: Graph = points (x,y) satisfying y=p(x). Linear → straight line, cuts X-axis at exactly one point. Quadratic → parabola U (a>0 up, a<0 down), can cut X-axis at 0,1,2 points. y=xⁿ: as n↑ steeper, odd n in I & III quadrants, even in I & II, y=-xⁿ is reflection. Geographically, zero = where graph cuts X-axis.
sections.visual: Linear line, quadratic U (a>0 2 points, a>0 1 point, a<0 0 points), y=xⁿ family morph, 3-min movie

sections.title: Zeroes — p(k)=0
sections.content: k is zero if p(k)=0. Example p(x)=x²-3x+2, p(1)=1-3+2=0 → 1 is zero. Geometrically, zero = X-intercept. Degree n has at most n zeroes: linear 1, quadratic ≤2, cubic ≤3.
sections.visual: p(1) calc → 0, then X-intercept A,B,C for linear/quadratic/cubic, 20s

sections.title: Factorisation — Splitting Middle Term
sections.visual: Middle term split as -2-3, grouping 2x(x-1) and -3(x-1), factor (x-1) highlighted, garden grouping

sections.title: Relationship — Zeroes & Coefficients
sections.content: Quadratic ax²+bx+c with α,β: α+β=-b/a (sum = -coeff x / coeff x²), αβ=c/a (product = constant / coeff x²). Cubic ax³+bx²+cx+d with α,β,γ: α+β+γ=-b/a, αβ+βγ+γα=c/a, αβγ=-d/a. Example 9x²-16x+20: a=9,b=-16,c=20 → sum 16/9, product 20/9.
sections.visual: Formula cards: -b/a and c/a with a,b,c highlighted, example 9x²-16x+20 → 16/9 & 20/9

sections.title: Division Algorithm
sections.content: For P(x), G(x)≠0, exists Q,R with P=G·Q+R, deg R < deg G. Steps: arrange descending, divide highest term, remainder becomes next dividend, repeat until deg R < deg G. Like long division with polynomials.
sections.visual: Long division ladder: P → Q,R, remainder highlighted, 20s

sections.title: Algebraic Identities
sections.content: (a+b)²=a²+2ab+b², (a-b)²=a²-2ab+b², (x+a)(x+b)=x²+(a+b)x+ab, a²-b²=(a+b)(a-b), a³±b³, (a±b)³ — all via garden area/volume.
sections.visual: Area model: (a+b)² as square a² + 2ab + b², 3D for cubes

solvedExamples.q: Determine quadratic polynomial with zeroes 5-3√2 and 5+3√2
solvedExamples.solution: Sum =10, Product = (5)²-(3√2)²=25-18=7 → P(x)=x²-10x+7. Via (a+b)(a-b)=a²-b². Visual: sum 10 as 5+5, product 7 as 25-18.

solvedExamples.q: Find zeroes of 6x²-3-7x and verify relationship
solvedExamples.solution: 6x²-7x-3=0 → 6x²-9x+2x-3=0 → 3x(2x-3)+1(2x-3)=0 → (3x+1)(2x-3)=0 → x=-1/3, 3/2. Verify: sum 7/6 = -b/a, product -1/2 = c/a. Visual: grouping 3x and 1.

sections.title: Graphical Method — Where Lines Meet
sections.content: Two lines a1x+b1y=c1, a2x+b2y=c2. Plot each: table of 2 points, join. Cases: a1/a2≠b1/b2 → intersect at one point (unique, e.g., 2x+3y=11 & 2x-4y=-24 meet at (-2,5)); a1/a2=b1/b2≠c1/c2 → parallel (no solution, e.g., 3x+ky=7,6x+4y=8 with k=2); a1/a2=b1/b2=c1/c2 → coincident (infinite, e.g., x+y=2,2x+2y=4). Visual: 3 graphs side-by-side, U with intersection highlighted, parallel never meet, coincident overlap. Daily: two shop bills → price of pen/book. Frontier: air traffic paths intersect? → linear systems for GPS.
sections.visual: Garden diagram for Graphical Method — Where Lines Meet — 3-min movie-like, 3D, real-life

sections.title: Substitution — Express & Replace
sections.content: Solve one equation for y (or x), substitute into other, solve single variable, back-substitute. Example: y=2x, 3x+y=10 → 3x+2x=10 → x=2,y=4. Works best when one variable has coefficient 1. Visual: y=2x as see-saw, substitute as replacing weight.
sections.visual: Garden diagram for Substitution — Express & Replace — 3-min movie-like, 3D, real-life

sections.title: Elimination — Make Equal, Add/Subtract
sections.content: Multiply to make coefficients of one variable equal, then add/subtract to eliminate. Example: 2x+3y=11 (×2), 2x-4y=-24 → subtract → 7y=35 → y=5, x=-2. Golden Step: choose variable with LCM smallest. Visual: scales balancing, eliminating one pan.
sections.visual: Garden diagram for Elimination — Make Equal, Add/Subtract — 3-min movie-like, 3D, real-life

sections.title: Cross-Multiplication — Fastest for MCQs
sections.content: Formula: x/(b1c2-b2c1)=y/(c1a2-c2a1)=1/(a1b2-a2b1). Example: 3x+2y=7,4x+5y=13 → x/(2·13-5·7)=y/(7·4-13·3)=1/(3·5-4·2) → x/(26-35)=y/(28-39)=1/(15-8) → x=-9/7? Wait compute: 26-35=-9, 28-39=-11, 15-8=7 → x=-9/7, y=-11/7. Check: use elimination for verification. Visual: cross arrows, 30s MCQ trick.
sections.visual: Garden diagram for Cross-Multiplication — Fastest for MCQs — 3-min movie-like, 3D, real-life

sections.title: Factorisation — Split Middle Term
sections.content: For 2x²-5x+3, middle -5x = -2x-3x where (-2)(-3)=6=2·3. So 2x²-2x-3x+3=2x(x-1)-3(x-1)=(x-1)(2x-3) → x=1,3/2. Visual: grouping 2x and -3, factor (x-1) highlighted.
sections.visual: Garden diagram for Factorisation — Split Middle Term — 3-min movie-like, 3D, real-life

sections.title: Quadratic Formula — Complete Square
sections.content: Derivation: ax²+bx+c=0 → a(x²+b/a x)=-c → a(x+b/2a)² = (b²-4ac)/4a → x=(-b±√(b²-4ac))/2a. Example 2x²+x-4 → D=33 → x=(-1±√33)/4. Visual: swing U-curve, vertex (-b/2a,-D/4a).
sections.visual: Garden diagram for Quadratic Formula — Complete Square — 3-min movie-like, 3D, real-life

sections.title: Discriminant — Nature of Roots
sections.content: D=b²-4ac: D>0 two distinct (swing kisses grass twice), D=0 one (kiss), D<0 none (fly high, imaginary). Example x²+kx+4 equal → D=k²-16=0 → k=±4. Visual: D as swing height.
sections.visual: Garden diagram for Discriminant — Nature of Roots — 3-min movie-like, 3D, real-life

sections.content: Area with fixed fence, profit peak at vertex -b/2a, rocket max height h(t)=-4.9t²+vt at vertex. Visual: farm rectangle, rocket trajectory.

unveiling.hook: Hook for Ch15 Probability: A real question — e.g., 'How do we know when two buses meet again? When does a swing just kiss the grass? How does a toy car swerve on carpet?'

unveiling.narrative: Concept unveiled for Ch15 Probability in three layers: 1) See — garden analogy with precise diagram, 2) Do — NCERT definition with first-principles measurement, 3) Prove — theorem derived with aligned LaTeX, each step justified, not just stated.

steps: Step 1 — Setup: Define with garden diagram (e.g., swing U-curve, ladder against wall, toy car marble→carpet)
Step 2 — First principles: Use NCERT definition, no hand-waving
Step 3 — Proof: Aligned LaTeX, each equality justified (e.g., complete square, area ratios, Snell via wave slowing)
Step 4 — Conclude: Boxed result, plus why this proof matters for the next chapter (e.g., D → nature of roots → Class XI quadratic inequalities)
derivation.visual: Split-screen 3-min: left 3D garden builds step-by-step, right LaTeX proof highlights on hover — 3-min distilled
